title: T1490 — Inhibit System Recovery
subtitle: Watch the attack unfold step by step on a compromised file server.

steps.title: OF 8 - STOLEN ADMIN LOGON
steps.caption: The attacker signs in to FILE01 with an admin account stolen by an infostealer. Nothing looks broken yet, but they now control the backups.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Compare RDP logon sources with your known admin jump hosts and alert on the rest.

steps.title: OF 8 - PRIVILEGE CHECK
steps.caption: The attacker runs whoami /priv to confirm they hold admin rights. Deleting shadow copies and editing boot settings both require this level.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Flag admin utilities started from interactive sessions that are not your jump hosts.

steps.title: OF 8 - LIST THE SAFETY NETS
steps.caption: The attacker lists every shadow copy on the server. This is reconnaissance: they are measuring how much recovery data they are about to destroy.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Shadow copy enumeration on a server outside a backup job is an early warning worth an alert.

steps.title: OF 8 - DELETE ALL SHADOW COPIES One silent comma
steps.caption: nd wipes every restore point on the host. The shadow copy store empties within seconds and local rollback is gone.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Alert at high severity on any delete-shadows command, and page when a server matches.

steps.caption: r deletes the backup catalog. The backup files may survive on disk, but Windows no longer knows they exist, so restore tooling goes blind.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Any wbadmin delete catalog event should map to a change ticket. No ticket means page the on-call analyst.

steps.title: OF 8 - BREAK RECOVERY BOOT
steps.caption: The attacker disables the Windows recovery environment with bcdedit. After the next reboot, the built-in repair options will not start at all.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Watch for bcdedit recoveryenabled changes outside golden image provisioning hosts.

steps.title: OF 8 - THE SOC CONNECTS THE DOTS
steps.caption: The SIEM correlates three events from one host and one user in five minutes and raises a single critical incident for T1490. The attack is now impossible to ignore.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Build this correlation rule before the attack happens, and include host and user in the alert context.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: OF 8 - ISOLATE AND RESTORE
steps.caption: The SOC isolates FILE01, blocks the stolen account, and restores data from the immutable backup copy the attacker could never reach. The attack fails here.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Keep one backup copy offline or immutable, and prove every quarter that you can restore from it.
